title: Eldora Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Eldora wells have a 140 ft median depth, 7.0 gpm median yield, and typical finished costs of $15,100-$26,000.
h1: Eldora, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Buying land near Eldora means dealing with mountain bedrock, not a uniform shallow groundwater system. DWR records within 5 miles show 723 permitted wells, including 515 recorded as constructed. Of the wells reporting depth, the median is 140 feet, but the range is wide enough that a neighboring well is useful evidence, not a guarantee.

Most permits are for domestic or household use, and the named geology is usually unnamed fractured bedrock. The practical questions are how far a driller may need to go, how much water the formation can produce, and what the complete well installation will cost.

sections.heading: How deep are wells around Eldora?
sections.html:
Eldora wells have a median reported depth of 140 feet. The middle half runs from 40 to 260 feet, meaning many wells fall in that band, while the 90th percentile reaches 400 feet. The deepest well in these records is 800 feet.

The depth mix shows the spread clearly: 41% are under 100 feet, 37% are between 100 and 300 feet, 21% are between 300 and 600 feet, and 2% are deeper than 600 feet. This is fractured mountain bedrock, identified on most permits as unnamed fractured-bedrock aquifer. Granite and gneiss can carry water in cracks rather than in a predictable continuous layer. For a bid, use 140 feet only as a planning reference. A driller should review nearby logs, access, casing and grouting needs before giving a firm price.

sections.heading: What water yield can a home expect?
sections.html:
Among the 201 Eldora-area records that report pump yield, the median is 7.0 gallons per minute. The middle half is 5.0 to 10.0 gallons per minute, and 70% report yields from 5 to 15 gallons per minute. Another 20% fall between 1 and 5 gallons per minute, while 9% report more than 15 gallons per minute. Only 1% are under 1 gallon per minute.

That distribution is generally workable for a household, but a reported pumping rate is not the same as unlimited storage. A low-producing well can still serve a home if the well, pump controls and storage are designed appropriately. Ask for the original yield test and permit file. Colorado exempt household-use wells also have a 35 gpm pumping limit, so the permitted use matters.

sections.heading: Water levels and the local groundwater trend
sections.html:
Only 34 wells in the Eldora records report a static water level, so the water-level sample is much smaller than the depth sample. Those reported levels have a median of 36 feet below the surface, with the middle half from 16 to 50 feet.

The decade comparison does not show a simple falling water table in this dataset. The median measured level was 50 feet below surface in the 2010s and 32 feet in the 2020s. Because the measurements come from different wells and locations, that change should not be treated as a regional forecast. A water level is also not the same as well depth: a 140-foot well may encounter water at a much shallower point. Before buying, request the well construction report, static level, pump test and any recent service information for the specific property.

sections.heading: Who has drilled near Eldora, and when?
sections.html:
Permit activity around Eldora spans several decades. Records show 7 permits in the 1950s, 44 in the 1960s, 128 in the 1970s, 95 in the 1980s, 146 in the 1990s, 94 in the 2000s, 63 in the 2010s and 20 in the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025. This history shows long-term residential well development rather than a short burst of construction.

The most frequently represented drillers are Ground Water Systems Inc (Wilson, Richard R.) with 111 records, C R Smith Drilling Inc (Smith, Frank) with 83, and C. R. Smith Drilling (Smith, Calvin R.) with 54. Those records can help identify local drilling history, but they are not a recommendation. Compare the construction reports for nearby lots in Eldora, Nederland and Rollinsville before selecting a contractor.

sections.heading: What does a new well cost in Eldora?
sections.html:
The local cost model is based on fractured mountain bedrock, including granite and gneiss. Drilling is estimated at $65-$100 per foot. At the 140-foot median depth, the drilled hole comes to about $9,100-$14,000.

That is not the complete water-system price. A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching and electrical is estimated at $15,100-$26,000 at the median depth. A deeper hole moves the price upward, and difficult mountain access can affect the work even when depth is unchanged. The 40-to-260-foot middle-half depth range is important when comparing bids: a quote based on a shallow assumption may not cover the actual drilling risk. Get the scope in writing, including casing, grout, pump equipment, testing, trenching and electrical.

sections.heading: Eldora risks to check before building
sections.html:
The principal water risk is variability in fractured bedrock. Some wells produce well, while others require deeper drilling, storage planning or may not meet a household’s needs. A dry hole is a real construction risk in this geology, so review neighboring logs and ask how the contractor handles unsuccessful drilling.

Environmental history also deserves a site-specific review. Within about 10 miles, the map includes 12 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 1,095 historic mine features and 7 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Their presence does not prove contamination at a parcel. Test the well water and check the location of mine features, drainage and any prior land use. Septic design, well separation, steep access, trench routes and the building footprint should be evaluated together before finalizing a lot.

sections.heading: A practical plan for an Eldora lot
sections.html:
Start with the Colorado DWR permit and construction records for the property, then compare wells on nearby roads rather than relying on a countywide average. Look for depth, yield, static level, casing, grout and the aquifer description. The records are dominated by household use, at 87%, so they provide useful residential context for a home purchase.

For a new build, have the driller, septic designer and excavator review the same site plan. Confirm truck access, a drilling location, pump and electrical routes, storage needs, septic setbacks and the location of the house. Nearby Nederland and Rollinsville can provide additional local comparison points, but Eldora’s fractured granite and gneiss still make the parcel-specific well log the best evidence. Do not waive water testing or well-performance review simply because a neighboring property has a productive well.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Eldora?

A finished well including pump, tank, trenching and electrical is estimated at $15,100-$26,000. Deeper drilling and difficult access can increase the project cost.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Eldora?
faq.a: The mapped area includes 12 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 1,095 historic mine features and 7 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites within about 10 miles. That does not establish contamination at a particular property. Test the well water, review prior land use and check mine features and drainage before drinking it.

faq.q: Are Eldora wells getting deeper or running out of water?
faq.a: The available water-level data do not show a simple dropping trend. Median static water level was 50 feet below surface in the 2010s and 32 feet in the 2020s, based on 34 reported measurements. The samples come from different wells, so they are not a regional forecast. Review the property’s own static level and yield test.
